title: Smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture
attempt: Computed the critical points and pole-chart Hessians of the height function on the standard unit sphere S4 in R5, making the simplest handle certificate explicit.
result: There are exactly two critical points. Their Hessians are I4 and −I4, so the Morse indices are 0 and 4 and the associated handle description has one handle of each index.
scope_limit: This verifies the standard sphere only; it extracts no certificate for an arbitrary homotopy sphere or a published four-dimensional candidate.
next_decision: Retain this calibration; a candidate-specific proof needs an actual handle description and justified simplifications.

title: Smooth four-dimensional Schoenflies conjecture
attempt: Constructed explicit parametrizations of both closed hemispheres bounded by the standard equatorial S3 in S4, and checked the sphere equation and inverses algebraically.
result: Each hemisphere is smoothly diffeomorphic to the closed four-ball. The denominator in the inverse is at least one on its matching hemisphere, including the boundary.
scope_limit: The embedding is the standard equator. This gives no straightening map for a general smooth embedded three-sphere.
next_decision: Use these maps to validate boundary conventions before attempting a nonstandard embedding.

title: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
attempt: Built a balanced two-generator presentation using eight elementary Andrews–Curtis moves from the trivial presentation, then executed and logged every inverse move with exact free reduction.
result: The resulting presentation reduces back to the ordered relators x and y. The saved certificate contains the starting words, all eight reducing moves, and every intermediate state.
evidence: geometry_calculations.py: apply_move, inverse_move, reduce_word; item 58 contains the replayable word certificate.
scope_limit: This deliberately generated example is known trivial by construction. No hard published candidate or stabilization question was resolved.
next_decision: The move checker is ready; the next substantive input must be an independently specified candidate presentation.

title: Slice–ribbon conjecture
attempt: Examined the explicit disk (u,v,0,0) inside the unit four-ball and computed the radial Morse function to certify the ribbon condition for its boundary unknot.
result: The restricted squared radius is u²+v². Its only interior critical point is a nondegenerate minimum; there are no interior maxima. Thus the disk is an explicit ribbon disk.
scope_limit: This solves only the unknot calibration and says nothing about a nontrivial slice candidate. No failed search is being interpreted as non-ribbonness.
next_decision: Move to a specified slice knot only after its slicing certificate and diagram are available.

title: Crossing-number additivity conjecture
attempt: Multiplied the trefoil Jones polynomial by itself using exact integer convolution, then compared its breadth with the six-crossing connected-sum diagram.
result: The product has lowest exponent 2 and highest exponent 8. Jones breadth gives a lower bound of six crossings, matching the diagram upper bound, so two trefoils have additive crossing number.
scope_limit: This is a familiar alternating example. The polynomial breadth need not attain crossing number for general knots.
next_decision: Retain this exact control; a wider proof needs a lower bound effective when Jones breadth is deficient.

title: Purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in the three-sphere
attempt: Derived the first homology of Dehn filling and applied it to every reduced slope p/q with −4≤p≤4 and 1≤q≤4.
result: There are 23 slopes and 253 unordered pairs. Different absolute numerators eliminate 198 pairs for every knot; 55 pairs survive this necessary homological filter.
evidence: H1(S3_{p/q}(K);Z)=Z/pZ because the longitude vanishes in exterior homology and filling kills pμ; p=0 gives Z.
scope_limit: Equal homology does not imply homeomorphism, and the surviving pairs are not verified cosmetic surgeries. The filter ignores orientation-sensitive invariants.
next_decision: Apply stronger surgery invariants only to surviving pairs for a specified knot.

title: Volume conjecture
attempt: Evaluated the figure-eight colored Jones root-of-unity product formula at N=20,40,80 using independently repeated 70-digit and 130-digit Decimal calculations.
result: The scaled logarithms are approximately 3.36473742636, 2.85816821563, and 2.52511086864. Both precision runs agree within 10^−65; these finite values remain above the known volume 2.02988321282.
scope_limit: Precision agreement is numerical validation, not a rigorous interval enclosure. Three terms do not prove convergence, and the figure-eight case is already known.
next_decision: Use this normalization control before evaluating a new knot; do not extrapolate a proof from the trend.

title: 11/8 conjecture
attempt: Translated the 11/8 inequality and the older Furuta 10/8+2 inequality into exact integer conditions for forms 2k(−E8)⊕lH, then tabulated k=1 through 8.
result: The target becomes l≥3k, while the older bound gives l≥2k+1. The interval between them contains 28 pairs in this finite table; k=1 has no gap.
scope_limit: These are arithmetic gaps in one older bound, not realizable manifolds or a list of currently undecided forms. Stronger known restrictions were deliberately not applied.
next_decision: Any realizability investigation must first apply the strongest known form-specific obstructions.

title: Borel rigidity conjecture
attempt: Proved the torus-to-torus case directly using equivariant lifts and checked an explicit five-dimensional integral automorphism and its inverse by exact matrix multiplication.
result: A homotopy equivalence f:Tn→Tn inducing A∈GL(n,Z) is homotopic to the linear homeomorphism induced by A. The straight-line homotopy of lifts respects every integer translation.
evidence: H_s(x)=(1−s)F(x)+sAx; H_s(x+z)=H_s(x)+Az; saved 5×5 matrices satisfy AA^−1=I.
scope_limit: Both manifolds here are tori. This does not prove rigidity for an arbitrary manifold merely homotopy equivalent to a torus, or for other aspherical manifolds.
next_decision: Keep the lift argument as a control; the missing step is geometric identification of a general source manifold.

title: Novikov conjecture
attempt: Worked out every possible higher signature in dimension two, where positive-degree components of the Hirzebruch L-class cannot contribute.
result: For closed oriented surfaces and an orientation-preserving homotopy equivalence h, naturality of cohomology pairing proves the required equality for every degree-two group-cohomology class; all other degrees contribute zero.
scope_limit: This is the elementary surface case. It does not control positive-degree L-classes in higher dimensions or establish the general conjecture.
next_decision: Any extension must address those higher characteristic classes rather than reuse dimension-two vanishing.

title: Farrell–Jones conjecture
attempt: Specialized the Farrell–Jones assembly map to the infinite dihedral group and checked its explicit semidirect-product relation.
result: The group Z⋊C2 contains Z with index two, so it is virtually cyclic. Consequently a point is a model for E_VCyc(G), and the assembly map is literally the identity.
scope_limit: This is an immediate known base case, not a new assembly calculation for a group outside the virtually cyclic family.
next_decision: A nontrivial next attempt needs a specified group for which E_VCyc(G) is not already a point.

title: Inverse Galois problem over the rational numbers
attempt: Constructed an explicit rational polynomial realization of the finite group S3 and checked the two decisive algebraic conditions.
result: The polynomial x³−2 is Eisenstein at 2, hence irreducible. Its discriminant is −108, which is not a rational square; the transitive cubic Galois group is therefore S3.
scope_limit: This is a standard realization of one already realizable group. It supplies no construction for arbitrary finite groups and no new regular extension.
next_decision: Use this example to validate a Galois-group certificate format before choosing a genuinely unresolved group-realization target.

title: Tate conjecture
attempt: Enumerated the split quadric x0x1−x2x3=0 over F7 and combined its point count with the intersection pairing of its two rational rulings.
result: Exactly 64 of the 400 projective points lie on the quadric. Its two rulings have intersection matrix [[0,1],[1,0]], hence independent classes; the product P1×P1 description shows they span H².
evidence: #Q(F7)=64=(7+1)²; det intersection matrix=−1; both ruling cycles are defined over F7 with Qℓ coefficients, ℓ≠7.
scope_limit: This proves the divisor Tate statement for this split quadric using its known product decomposition, not from point counts alone.
next_decision: A non-split surface requires actual Frobenius and cycle calculations instead of this product argument.

title: Lefschetz standard conjecture
attempt: Computed the Lefschetz operator for the complex abelian surface E×E with product polarization, then supplied algebraic correspondences realizing its inverse.
result: In the saved bases H1→H3 is a permutation matrix squaring to identity. Integration on either elliptic factor, represented by E×E times the other diagonal, gives inverse correspondences whose sum inverts this map.
evidence: h=a1∧b1+a2∧b2; h²=2a1∧b1∧a2∧b2. The H4→H0 inverse has coefficient 1/2.
scope_limit: This verifies one complex product-polarized surface. Matrix inversion alone would not suffice without the exhibited algebraic cycles.
next_decision: Retain the correspondence certificate; extending to other varieties requires analogous algebraic inverse operators.

title: Abundance conjecture
attempt: Derived the canonical section counts on X=C×C×E×E, with genus-two C given by y²=x⁵−1 and elliptic E by y²=x³−x.
result: K_X pulls back the globally generated canonical bundle on C×C, hence is nef and semiample. Riemann–Roch and Künneth give h0(mK_X)=(2m−1)² for m≥2; m=0..6 yield 1,4,9,25,49,81,121.
evidence: h0(C,mK_C)=2m−1 for m≥2; h0(E,mK_E)=1; numerical dimension ν(K_X)=2.
scope_limit: This is an explicit product fourfold. Its canonical map at m=1 includes genus-two hyperelliptic maps; it is not an embedding of C×C.
next_decision: Use the exact count as a control; a non-product nef canonical divisor needs a different semiampleness argument.

title: Termination of flips conjecture
attempt: Tested the logical inference that a strictly decreasing nonnegative real progress measure would force every flip sequence to terminate.
result: The exact recurrence x0=1 and x_(n+1)=x_n/(1+x_n) gives x_n=1/(n+1). Eleven values were computed as fractions, and induction proves an infinite strictly decreasing positive sequence.
evidence: x_n−x_(n+1)=1/((n+1)(n+2))>0; inf x_n=0 is never reached.
scope_limit: These numbers are not flips or discrepancies of constructed varieties. The calculation rejects an insufficient termination argument, not the termination conjecture.
next_decision: A proposed geometric measure must also have a proved well-founded value set or another finite-descent mechanism.

title: Nagata’s conjecture on plane curves
attempt: Built exact jet-interpolation matrices for ten explicit integer points and equal multiplicities m=1,2,3, taking maximum prohibited degrees d=3,6,9.
result: The matrices have ranks 10/10, 28/28, and 55/55. Independently evaluated square minors modulo 1009 are 6,984,183; their nonvanishing certifies full column rank in characteristic zero.
evidence: Points Pi=(i,(i²+i⁵) mod101), i=0..9; geometry_interpolation_certificates.json records every row, column, and selected minor.
scope_limit: This proves the indicated three multiplicities for very general ten points by openness, including lower degrees by inclusion. It covers neither all multiplicities nor arbitrary point counts.
next_decision: Keep the exact minors; future work must introduce an argument controlling unbounded multiplicity.

title: Segre–Harbourne–Gimigliano–Hirschowitz conjecture
attempt: Executed three mixed-multiplicity interpolation tests on ten points and a two-double-point special-case control, with exact modular minor certificates.
result: For (d;m)=(4;2,1⁹),(4;2²,1⁸),(5;2⁵,1⁵), vector-space dimensions are 3,1,1. The conic control has dimension one, with explicit generator (y−2x)² and rank five.
evidence: geometry_interpolation_certificates.json; in the control E=H−E1−E2, E²=−1, D=2E and D·E=−2.
scope_limit: The first three maximal-rank results hold for very general points. The special control uses eight zero multiplicities and verifies a familiar doubled-line mechanism only.
next_decision: Use these positive and negative controls before interpreting a rank defect in a broader mixed system.

title: Hopf’s positive-curvature Euler-characteristic conjecture
attempt: Evaluated the six-dimensional Euler form under constant positive sectional curvature, counting its Pfaffian pairings and checking the unit-sphere integral exactly.
result: There are 15 pairings. The Euler density is 15κ³/(8π³) times volume, which is positive when κ>0. Multiplying by Vol(S6)=16π³/15 at κ=1 gives Euler characteristic two.
scope_limit: This covers constant-curvature six-manifolds via Gauss–Bonnet. Variable positive sectional curvature does not make this substitution legitimate.
next_decision: A broader argument must control the full curvature tensor in the Euler polynomial.

title: Hopf’s S2 × S2 problem
attempt: Applied the exact conformal sectional-curvature formula at a global minimum of an arbitrary smooth conformal factor on the standard product S2×S2.
result: Every metric e^(2f)g_product has a plane with nonpositive curvature: choose a mixed plane at the minimum, where df=0 and Hess f is positive semidefinite. Thus no conformal deformation, of any amplitude, achieves everywhere positive curvature.
evidence: K_new(X∧Y)=e^(−2f)[−Hess f(X,X)−Hess f(Y,Y)]≤0 at the minimum.
scope_limit: Only the conformal class of the standard product metric is excluded. General nonconformal metrics remain outside the argument.
next_decision: Discard this conformal search family as a route to a positively curved counterexample.

title: Chern’s isoparametric conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces
attempt: Constructed and checked a nonzero formal first-derivative tensor for principal curvatures (−3,−1,1,3), enforcing symmetry, differentiated mean/scalar constraints, and the scalar Simons norm identity.
result: The tensor satisfies those necessary constraints with S=20 and |∇A|²=320, yet ∇K=(48√5,0,0,0). Therefore the proposed shortcut from these pointwise constraints to constant Gauss–Kronecker curvature fails.
evidence: T111=2√5; symmetric T122=−4√5; symmetric T133=2√5; remaining entries zero. |T|²=S(S−4).
scope_limit: This formal jet is not a constructed local immersion or compact hypersurface. Higher-order compatibility and global realization were not proved.
next_decision: Any repaired argument must use constraints beyond this verified first-derivative system.

title: Symmetric Mahler conjecture in dimensions four and higher
attempt: Derived exact primal and polar volumes for K_t=conv(±e1,…,±e4,±t(1,1,1,1)), throughout t≥1/2, using visible pyramids and clipped-cube integration.
result: The volumes are t+1/4 and 32/(3t)−4/(3t³)+1/(4t⁴). Their product exceeds 32/3 because its gap has an explicitly positive polynomial numerator. At t=1 the product is 575/48.
scope_limit: This proves the bound for one stated centrally symmetric polytope family, not all four-dimensional bodies. No novelty claim is made.
next_decision: Remove this family from counterexample searches; a wider proof needs control beyond its special diagonal symmetry.

title: Zariski cancellation problem in characteristic zero
attempt: Tested whether the kernel of one convenient locally nilpotent derivation can canonically identify a coordinate in the cancellation strategy.
result: On C[x,y,z]/(xy−z²+1), the explicit derivations δ=(0,2z,x) and ε=(2z,0,y) both preserve the relation and are locally nilpotent. Yet x lies in ker δ while ε(x)=2z≠0.
evidence: δ(xy−z²+1)=ε(xy−z²+1)=0; δ³y=ε³x=0; saved generator chains certify local nilpotence.
scope_limit: This surface calculation refutes the single-derivation invariance shortcut. It is not a counterexample to cancellation of complex affine three-space.
next_decision: A canonical invariant must account for all relevant derivations or extra justified structure.

title: Bounded negativity conjecture in characteristic zero
attempt: Specified ten distinct points (i,i²,1) on the smooth projective conic yz−x²=0 and computed the strict transform after blowing up those points.
result: The resulting fixed smooth projective surface contains an irreducible rational curve C with C²=−6. Its canonical intersection is four, and adjunction gives genus zero. Any negativity bound for this surface is at least six.
scope_limit: One negative curve on one fixed surface does not violate bounded negativity. Allowing the number of blowups to vary changes the surface.
next_decision: Further attempts must seek an unbounded sequence on this same fixed surface, not move the ambient surface.

title: Four-dimensional sphere-packing problem
attempt: Verified D4 covolume two and its 24 shortest vectors, then moved one coset in a two-coset description by s times the first coordinate vector.
result: The original density is π²/16. Two explicit inter-coset vectors give squared minimum distance at most 2−2|s|+s²<2 for 0<|s|<2. At fixed cell volume, rescaling spheres therefore lowers density along this path.
evidence: D4=L∪(b1+L), L=⟨2b1,b2,b3,b4⟩; vectors ±b1+se1 certify the bound.
scope_limit: This is one explicit periodic perturbation control, consistent with known periodic extremality. It neither searches all finite deformations nor proves global packing optimality.
next_decision: Exclude this displacement path from improvement searches; different finite deformations require new certificates.
